title: Milestone: The Solar System
objective: After this level you can connect the planets, moons and small bodies into one picture of our solar system.
summary: From the Sun’s 99.8% of the mass to Neptune 30 AU out, the solar system is one family shaped by gravity.

cards.headline: Milestone: halfway to Mastery. Let’s put the whole solar system in one picture.
cards.body: Back in Level 1 you wrote Earth's address. Now zoom out and see the whole neighborhood at once, from the Sun to Neptune: one family of worlds, all held together by the Sun's gravity.

cards.headline: How big is our neighborhood?
cards.body: Neptune orbits about 30 astronomical units from the Sun, about 4.5 billion km. That number is too big to feel, so use light instead. Sunlight reaches Earth in about 8 minutes. To reach Neptune, it needs about 4 hours. Leave the Sun with the light at breakfast, and you'd arrive at Neptune around lunch.

cards.headline: Where the mass is: one giant and a lot of crumbs

items.label: The Sun
points: Its gravity holds every planet and smaller body in orbit

items.label: Everything else
points: About 0.2%: planets, moons, asteroids and comets
Jupiter alone is more than twice all the other planets combined

cards.headline: Milestone: solar system mapped
learned: The Sun holds 99.8% of the mass
Jupiter outweighs all other planets combined
Sunlight takes about 4 hours to reach it

questions.prompt: About what share of the solar system’s mass is in the Sun?

options.label: About half of it
options.rationale: Far more than half.

options.label: About 75 percent of it
options.rationale: Still far too low.

options.label: About 90 percent of it
options.rationale: Close, but it’s even more.

questions.explanation: The Sun holds about 99.8% of the solar system’s mass; everything else shares the last 0.2%.

questions.prompt: What gives Mars its red color?

options.label: Iron oxide, like rust, in its dust and rocks
Red algae growing in its soil
options.rationale: There is no known life on Mars.

options.label: The light of a red sun in its sky
options.rationale: Mars orbits our own Sun.

options.label: Hot lava glowing on its surface
options.rationale: Mars’s volcanoes are inactive today.

questions.explanation: Iron oxide, the same compound as rust, coats Martian dust and rocks.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Jupiter’s mass is true?

options.label: It weighs about the same as Saturn
options.rationale: Jupiter is about three times more massive than Saturn.

options.label: It is more than twice all other planets combined
It is lighter than the Earth
options.rationale: Jupiter is far more massive than Earth.

options.label: It is heavier than the Sun itself
options.rationale: The Sun holds 99.8% of the mass.

questions.explanation: Jupiter has more than twice the mass of all the other planets combined.

questions.prompt: What are Saturn’s rings made of?

options.label: A single flat sheet of solid rock
options.rationale: The rings aren’t solid.

options.label: Glowing clouds of hot gas
options.rationale: The rings are cold chunks, not gas.

options.label: Countless chunks of mostly water ice
Dust blown off the Sun by the wind
options.rationale: The rings are mostly ice from Saturn’s surroundings.

questions.explanation: Saturn’s rings are countless separate chunks of mostly water ice, each orbiting Saturn on its own.

questions.prompt: Neptune is about 30 AU from the Sun. About how long does sunlight take to reach it?

options.label: About 8 minutes
options.rationale: That’s the time to reach Earth, 1 AU away.

options.label: About 30 minutes
options.rationale: Each AU takes about 8 minutes, not 1.

options.label: About 30 days
options.rationale: Light is far faster than that.

questions.explanation: Light takes about 8 minutes per AU, so 30 AU takes about 30 × 8 = 240 minutes: roughly 4 hours.

questions.prompt: Europa and Enceladus are far from the Sun’s heat. What keeps their hidden oceans liquid?

options.label: Thick atmospheres trapping heat
options.rationale: Neither has a thick atmosphere; that’s Titan.

options.label: Tidal flexing by their planets’ gravity
Sunlight reflected off their planets
options.rationale: Reflected light is far too weak.

options.label: Heat from nearby comets
options.rationale: Comets bring no lasting heat.

questions.explanation: Their giant planets’ gravity squeezes and flexes these moons, heating their interiors enough to keep water liquid.

questions.prompt: Besides Earth, which world has stable liquid on its surface?

options.label: Europa, under its thick ice
options.rationale: Europa’s ocean is beneath its ice, not on the surface.

options.label: Mars, in its ancient riverbeds
options.rationale: Those rivers dried up long ago.

options.label: Venus, beneath its acid clouds
options.rationale: Venus is far too hot for surface liquid.

questions.explanation: Titan is the only world besides Earth known to have stable liquid on its surface: lakes of methane and ethane.
